title: Rosalind and the Orbit
premise: Petra Yarrow has spent eleven years alone tending Earth's abandoned seed vault, recording the slow collapse of the Meridian colony on a moon no fleet ship will visit. When gravity stutters for nine seconds across the whole system, she wakes aboard the warship Vesperine, where the crew insists she is Lieutenant Rosalind Okafor — an officer who died in a massacre that, according to every official record, never happened. As fragments of Rosalind's memories surface in Petra's mind, she realizes the nine-second flicker was a weapon's test run by the fleet itself, and the truce keeping two armadas from open war expires in thirty days. To stop a second massacre, Petra must reconstruct erased evidence using only her caretaker's logs and Rosalind's buried recollections, while falling for the Vesperine's navigator, Idris Vale, who loved Rosalind and cannot decide whether Petra is a ghost or a second chance. In the end, Petra broadcasts the true records to both fleets at the cost of her own identity — the Rosalind memories overwrite her — but Idris carries Petra's seed-vault journals home to Earth, planting what she saved.
about_author: Odile Montrose is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing obsolete agricultural data before turning to fiction. She writes science fiction about people who keep records when no one else will.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Alone in the seed vault, Petra narrates her 4,000th daily log: dying colony signals, rotting seals, her own fraying mind. Then gravity fails for exactly nine seconds, and she falls upward into light. The chapter ends mid-fall, establishing loneliness shattered by the impossible. Emotional beat: quiet dread giving way to vertigo.

chapters.title: The Name They Give Me
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. She wakes restrained aboard the warship Vesperine; the crew calls her Lieutenant Rosalind Okafor, dead eleven months. Medical scans show memories that aren't hers bleeding into her mind — a woman laughing in a mess hall, a coded warning. Navigator Idris Vale watches her with grief he won't explain. Beat: disorientation and the first ache of borrowed love.

chapters.title: What the Records Refuse
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, with an interlude of fleet communiqués. She requests files on Rosalind's final mission to Meridian's moon and finds them sealed, then scrubbed — every record says the colony was evacuated successfully, yet Petra logged its death herself. Captain Serevan warns her to drop it before the truce expires. Beat: the first hard evidence of erasure.

chapters.title: Idris Teaches Me the Ship
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Assigned to menial duty, Petra shadows Idris through the Vesperine's corridors. He tests her with private details only Rosalind knew — a scar story, a song hummed off-key — and she answers correctly without knowing why. Their intimacy deepens uneasily; he mourns her even as he's drawn to her. Beat: tenderness tangled with guilt.

chapters.title: Rosalind's Last Transmission
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Rosalind's recovered log entries interleave with Petra decoding them. Rosalind discovered the fleet had tested a gravity-collapse weapon on Meridian's moon, killing 40,000 colonists, and hid the proof inside agricultural telemetry — the same format as Petra's vault logs. The flicker that took Petra was a second test. Beat: horror clicking into place.

chapters.title: The Truce Clock
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Twelve days remain. Serevan confines her after she confronts him; the fleet intends to blame Meridian's destruction on the rival armada once the truce lapses. Idris breaks her out of quarters, choosing Rosalind's cause over his oath. Beat: betrayal of institutions, trust between the two deepening into something neither will name.

chapters.title: Ghost in the Archive
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, hunted through the ship's maintenance levels. Using seed-vault indexing tricks, she hides encrypted evidence inside the ship's botanical life-support data — invisible to military sweeps. But each access of Rosalind's memories erodes more of Petra's own; she forgets her mother's face. Beat: sacrifice made literal, memory as currency.

chapters.title: Serevan's Reason
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Serevan and Petra. Cornered, the captain argues the lie prevents a war that would kill millions — one massacre concealed to prevent another. Petra counters that a peace built on forty thousand unmarked graves is already a war against the dead. He gives her until the truce ends. Beat: moral weight, no villains, only costs.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Climax. With Idris at the helm dodging both fleets' pickets, Petra transmits Rosalind's hidden telemetry and her own vault logs to every ship in the system as the truce expires. Fleets hold fire. But the memory bleed completes: Petra's self dissolves, and Rosalind Okafor opens her eyes on the bridge, remembering everything except the seed vault. Beat: triumph purchased with annihilation.

chapters.title: Seeds
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, coda. Months later, Rosalind — haunted by a life she lived only secondhand — travels to Earth's seed vault and finds Petra's handwritten journals, the one record of Petra that exists. Reading them, she chooses to carry both women forward, planting Petra's preserved seeds in thawing ground beside Idris. Beat: grief transmuted into continuation; memory kept by hand.
